svg.text: CLINICAL SIGNS OF HYPOXIA — RAT & BED-C
PA 2.2 · RAT = EARLY (COMPENSATION ACTIVE) · BED-C = LATE (ORGANS FAILING) · NEVER WAIT FOR CYANOSIS
EARLY SIGNS — RAT Mnemonic
Compensation is active — body is fighting back
R
Restlessness
Patient is fidgety, unable to settle. Sympathetic nervous system activation
from low O₂. Often misread as anxiety — it is hypoxia until proven otherwise.
Mechanism: ↓PaO₂ → chemoreceptor activation → sympathetic response
A
Anxiety
Sense of impending doom. Often occurs BEFORE obvious dyspnea. The brain
senses insufficient oxygen and triggers alarm.
Do NOT dismiss as "just anxiety" — check SpO₂ and O₂ delivery immediately.
T
Tachycardia (HR >100 bpm)
Heart pumps faster to increase cardiac output → more O₂ delivery per minute.
This IS compensation — the heart is compensating for lower O₂ content per beat.
Mechanism: DO₂ = CO × CaO₂ — if CaO₂ falls, CO rises to compensate.
T
Tachypnea (RR >20/min)
Chemoreceptors sense ↓PaO₂ or ↑PaCO₂ → drive faster breathing.
Lungs try to take in more O₂ and blow off CO₂.
Key sign: RR >20 with restlessness = intervene now, before it escalates.
LATE SIGNS — BED-C Mnemonic ⚠
Organs failing — immediate resuscitation required
B
Bradycardia — OMINOUS ⚠
Sudden HR DROP — the myocardium itself is hypoxic. Often precedes cardiac arrest.
Tachycardia → Bradycardia transition is an emergency signal.
Patient may appear deceptively "calmer" — they are actually in extremis.
E
Extreme Restlessness / Combativeness
Severe brain hypoxia → combative, thrashing, pulling out IVs. Not psychiatric behavior.
Patient may fight caregivers. Remove restraints and treat the hypoxia.
This is the brain suffocating — treat immediately.
D
Dyspnea — Labored Breathing
Visible, labored shortness of breath. Accessory muscle use, grunting, nasal flaring.
By this stage respiratory compensation is FAILING.
Dyspnea is a LATE sign — crisis intervention is needed immediately.
C
Cyanosis — Blue Discoloration
Blue lips, nail beds, skin. Requires ≥5 g/dL of deoxygenated Hb to appear visibly.
Extremely late sign. Often absent in anemia (not enough Hb to show blue color).
NEVER wait for cyanosis — intervene at RAT signs, not BED-C signs.
PulmoCore · PA 2.2 · Clinical Signs · RAT = Early (Restlessness, Anxiety, Tachycardia, Tachypnea) · BED-C = Late (Bradycardia, Extreme restlessness, Dyspnea, Cyanosis)
